rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Education Foundation of New Jersey (IEF) is a long-standing educational institution that has served the Muslim community since <cite id="1">its founding in 1983</cite>. The organization operates a comprehensive school system including <cite id="2">Al-Ghazaly Jr/Sr High School and Al-Hikmah Elementary School</cite>, providing religious and academic instruction from preschool through high school. In FY2025, the foundation reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $5,631,488</cite>, reflecting a <cite id="4">three-year revenue growth rate of 8.8%</cite>. While the organization maintains a <cite id="5">71.5% program expense ratio</cite> according to some filings, other data indicates a <cite id="6">program expense ratio of 71.5%</cite>, which falls below the <cite id="7">peer median of 89.8%</cite> for international education groups. The foundation focuses on high-quality instruction, evidenced by its <cite id="8">Cognia accreditation and an exceptional score of 352</cite>, which exceeds national averages. IEF serves approximately <cite id="9">621 beneficiaries</cite> with a model centered on capacity building through <cite id="10">179 to 183 instructional days per year</cite>. Financial stability is a notable strength, as the charity holds <cite id="11">16.3 months of working capital</cite>, ensuring it can sustain operations during economic shifts. However, the <cite id="12">cost per beneficiary is approximately $8,792.89</cite>, which is high for the sector and reflects the intensive nature of private school operations.
